messages:
maria: Heads-up — I merged the continuous-batching tweak to staging (max_batch_tokens=2048, window_ms=25). Need a lightweight throughput + tail-latency check before we flip canary. Can someone run ~1M tokens with loadgen (target ~1k qps)? Looking for median / p95 / p99 / p99.9 and any spikes >500ms. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4822

aj: I can run a quick pass tonight. Which model + payload distribution? small (<128 tokens) and mixed (avg 512) both? Also want 2 burst patterns: steady qps and intermittent 5x bursts.

devin: Use llama-2-7b-v3-qat on staging-cb-4a10 (same cluster as previous runs). I'll start with steady profile then run bursts. Command I use:```bash
./tools/loadgen --model llama-2-7b-v3-qat --qps 1000 --tokens 1000000 --payload-mix "small:40,mid:60" --concurrency 8 --run-id cb-stg-240123
```

infra-bot: Scheduled loadgen job cb-stg-240123 on staging-cb-4a10 (nodes=4) — run queued, estimated start in 10m. Job id: job-240123-1

sam: Run finished. Quick summary: QPS=980, median=28ms, p95=78ms, p99=210ms, p99.9=610ms. Observed ~3 spikes >800ms during a 90s window aligned with request arrival jitter. KV-cache hit rate ~86%.

leo: 610ms p99.9 is worrying. Any CPU/GPU saturation?

sam: GPU util ~72% steady, cpu on loadgen node spiked during one of the jitter windows. Logs show many small-batch fallbacks happening around the same time — we saw queue depth oscillate 12->2->14 in <200ms windows.

aj: That sounds like small-batch fallback thrash. Can we try disabling the fallback on a canary to isolate? Also we should capture per-request queuing timestamps.

maria: Agreed. Plan: A/B test — canary group with small_batch_fallback=false + window_ms=25 vs baseline. Collect same metrics + per-request queuing traces. @aj can you run?

aj: Starting A/B now. Disabling fallback for canary only and re-running loadgen (same params). Will attach traces to job.

infra-bot: A/B job scheduled: job-240123-2 (canary disabled fallback), job-240123-3 (baseline). ETA 8m.

devin: First A/B pass done. Results: baseline repeat roughly same. Canary (no fallback) QPS=970, median=31ms (+3ms), p95=82ms, p99=180ms, p99.9=320ms. No >500ms spikes observed during the same jitter windows. KV-cache hit rate unchanged.

leo: Nice — p99.9 320ms is much better. So fallback logic helps in average cases but under jitter it creates preemption thrash.

maria: Proposed mitigation: increase window_ms to 35 (wider coalescing) and keep fallback enabled. That should reduce oscillation while preserving small-batch safety. Can we do a quick smoke with window_ms=35 and fallback on?

aj: Running smoke with window_ms=35 now.

sam: Smoke results: QPS=975, median=30ms, p95=80ms, p99=190ms, p99.9=330ms. No >500ms spikes. Latency tradeoff small.

devin: Looks good. Action items: 1) update PR to set default window_ms=35 and add canary flag for fallback tuning (maria to approve), 2) add per-request queuing timestamps to tracing for next rollouts (aj), 3) schedule canary rollout at 03:00 PT (maria), 4) add a short post-canary smoke job to verify tail.

maria: I will update the PR with the default change and ping for review. Canary scheduled 03:00 PT. @devin please add a tiny doc snippet in the PR about why window_ms was increased.

leo: I'll open a quick follow-up to instrument queue timestamps in the trace collector.

aj: Pinged @eng-sre for on-call during the canary window.

maria: Great work team, thanks. :thumbsup: Will post the canary link once live and follow up with a short post-mortem if anything odd shows up.
